decisions.reason: As an organic variant of a core ham line, it fits the firm's stated organic expansion and can be carried with low incremental cost on existing processes.
This organic Kasseler extension remains close to the firm's cured-meat capabilities and strategy, though its demand is somewhat narrower than a standard ham item.
Organic pepper salami builds directly on established salami know-how and supports the organic range, so the option is still worth keeping at modest carrying cost.
The beef in teriyaki aspic appears to be a more experimental deli-counter specialty whose niche value should be clearer by now, making continued commitment less attractive.

Fennel-flavoured sliced salami is easy to make within the existing range but is a more niche taste for the firm's mainstream German deli customers, so rationalization is slightly more likely than retention.
The liver pâté with veal stays close to the firm's premium pâté business and existing expertise, so keeping it is still reasonable unless sales have clearly disappointed.
